signals.signal: NLB Group Annual Report 2025 states under the Group Payments workstream: 'Tenders for ATM and Cash Deposit Machines (CDS) were finalised.' No supplier is named anywhere in the 2025 annual report.
signals.implies: The single most actionable new fact this run: NLB ran and CLOSED Group-level tenders for both ATMs and merchant cash-deposit machines during 2025. Serbia's next self-service hardware and the CDS estate will be bought off those frameworks, so the buying decision that governs NLB Komercijalna's 304 ATMs has already been taken at Group level in Ljubljana, not in Belgrade. If Printec is not on that framework, Serbia-level selling has limited headroom; if it is, call-offs are the near-term revenue.
signals.likelihood: Call-offs against these frameworks are near-certain across 2026-2027
signals.followup: Establish urgently whether Printec bid or is on the NLB Group ATM and CDS frameworks awarded in 2025, who won, and the framework term. Escalate to Group procurement in Ljubljana, not the Serbian bank.

signals.signal: The bank's own live branch/ATM locator API returns 304 ATM records at 235 distinct addresses across 133 towns; 193 sit at branch addresses and 111 (36.5%) are off-branch/standalone. The bank also lists 129 branch locations across 84 towns, 91 standalone CDS cash-deposit stations and 1,627 partner merchant locations.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka branch & ATM locator (AEM facilities endpoint)
signals.implies: Precisely sizes the estate the 2022 'all 300 ATMs replaced' programme produced (baseline carried a round 300; the live figure is 304). The 111 off-branch units are the classic target for an ATM-as-a-service / managed-services wrap, and 2026 is year four of a 2022 fleet - the maintenance and refresh decision window.
signals.likelihood: High that a service/refresh decision falls within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Offer managed services benchmarking for the 111 off-branch ATMs; ask when the 2022 supply and maintenance contract expires.

signals.signal: Only 202 of the 304 ATMs accept cash deposits (RSD and EUR) - 102 units (34%) are cash-dispense-only. Off-branch units are the weakest: 76 of 111 take deposits and only 20 of 111 accept merchant 'pazar' takings, versus 110 of 193 at branch sites.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka branch & ATM locator (AEM facilities endpoint), cross-checked against the four published ATM-location PDFs
signals.implies: A hard, quantified white space of about 102 ATMs that cannot take cash in. A 'recycler' is a machine that re-dispenses deposited notes, cutting cash-in-transit runs and branch teller load. This maps straight to Printec cash automation / recyclers plus the ATM application work to drive deposit journeys, and it is the physical precondition for the bank's own >90%-off-branch target.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High: the end-2026 target is not reachable with a third of the fleet cash-out-only
signals.followup: Build a 102-unit recycler upgrade business case from the bank's own per-ATM capability list; quantify CIT and teller savings.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (market context for NLB Komercijalna)
signals.signal: NBS payment statistics for Q1 2026 (file updated 01/06/2026): ATM cash-DEPOSIT transactions on domestically issued cards 3,202,644 worth RSD 151,638m, versus 2,432,542 worth RSD 99,998m in Q1 2025 - +31.7% by count and +51.6% by value YoY. ATM withdrawals over the same period grew only +0.9% by count (24,793,602 vs 24,571,065).
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia - Payment transactions in the acceptance network by device type (trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)
signals.implies: Cash-IN, not cash-out, is the growth engine of the Serbian ATM channel: deposits are compounding at roughly 30% a year while withdrawals are flat. A bank with 102 dispense-only ATMs is structurally excluded from the only growing ATM volume. This is the strongest single argument for a recycler retrofit at NLB Komercijalna and across Serbian banks generally.
signals.likelihood: High that the trend persists through 2026-2027
signals.followup: Use this regulator series as the headline slide in the Serbian recycler pitch; refresh each quarter from the same NBS workbook.

signals.signal: NBS acceptance-network statistics: 3,336 ATMs in Serbia at end-Q1 2026, up from 3,265 at end-2025 and 3,219 at end-Q1 2025 (+3.6% YoY); 187,957 POS terminals (170,434 a year earlier, +10.3%); 5,948 virtual points of sale.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia - Acceptance network (prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)
signals.implies: Serbia's ATM estate is still GROWING, unlike Western Europe - the market backdrop supports new self-service placements rather than rationalisation. NLB Komercijalna's 304 ATMs are about 9.1% of the national fleet, roughly in line with its 10.2% asset share, so it is neither over- nor under-deployed and any growth must come from capability, not unit count. POS growth of +10.3% YoY sizes the acquiring opportunity.
signals.followup: Use the +3.6% ATM / +10.3% POS growth to frame Serbia as a placement market in the Printec regional plan.

signals.signal: NLB Group Annual Report 2025 records a Group-wide commitment 'to equip all ATMs with accessibility features by 2030', alongside compliance with the EU digital accessibility directive effective since June 2025. As at end-2025 only 58 ATMs in Slovenia supported voice-guided transactions for blind and partially sighted customers, with 26 more to be upgraded by Q1 2026; no equivalent figure is published for Serbia.
signals.source_name: NLB Group Annual Report 2025 (ENG), sustainability / financial inclusion chapter
signals.implies: A dated, board-level commitment that every one of NLB Komercijalna's 304 Serbian ATMs must gain accessibility features (audio jack, voice guidance, reachable UI) by 2030 - a compliance-driven refresh with a deadline, exactly the lever that carried Raiffeisen Romania's voice-guidance rollout. Printec self-service software and hardware retrofit both apply.
signals.likelihood: High over the 2026-2030 window; scoping work likely in the next 12 months
signals.followup: Ask NLB KB how many of its 304 ATMs already carry voice guidance and what the Serbian milestone plan to 2030 is.

signals.signal: Executive Board member for operations and IT Bojana Kalicanin-Stojanovic: the bank wants to end 2026 with the average client able to complete more than 90% of standard banking services without going to a branch, and states that two-thirds of its budget allocation goes into modern technology.
signals.implies: Re-verifies the baseline >90%-off-branch target with a named owner, a 2026 deadline and a stated budget skew. Achieving it needs deposit-capable self-service everywhere, remote onboarding/eKYC and 24/7 lobbies - Printec self-service, cash automation, digital onboarding and managed services all sit on the critical path.
signals.likelihood: High that related procurement activity lands in H2 2026
signals.followup: Take a gap analysis of the 90% target against the bank's own per-ATM capability data straight to the operations/IT board office.

signals.signal: Branch estate: NLB Group reports 139 branches at 31/03/2026 and the bank's own Pillar 3 disclosure reports 139 branches and 2,153 employees at 31/12/2025, but the public locator lists only 129 branch locations on 30/07/2026 - of which 52 have a 24/7 self-service zone, 85 have a CDS merchant cash-deposit device, 51 are flagged step-free for disabled access and just 6 still operate a day/night safe (DNT).
signals.source_name: NLB Group Interim Report January-March 2026; NLB KB 'Objavljivanje podataka i informacija' 31/12/2025; NLB KB locator
signals.implies: Only about 40% of branches have a 24/7 self-service zone - the clearest single build-out gap against the >90%-off-branch target and precisely the Printec 24/7 lobby / TCR proposition. The 129-vs-139 gap points to either a quiet net reduction of about ten units in H1 2026 or non-retail units excluded from the locator; either way the branch plan is live. The 6 surviving day/night safes are legacy manual drop-bag processes ripe for smart-safe replacement.
signals.followup: Reconcile 129 vs 139 with the bank; pitch 24/7 self-service zones for the roughly 77 branches that lack one.

signals.signal: Only 103 of 304 ATMs (34%) dispense EUR and 302 of 304 accept QR-code bill payment. Published limits: cash-in up to RSD 300,000 or EUR 3,000 per day for individuals; merchant takings capped at 150 banknotes per transaction and RSD 300,000 per day; EUR withdrawal minimum EUR 50, maximum EUR 1,000 per day; QR bill payment up to RSD 300,000.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka - Funkcionalnosti na bankomatima, plus the four published ATM-location PDFs (text extracted locally)
signals.implies: Two-thirds of the estate is single-currency dispense in a heavily euroised retail market, so a multi-currency cassette/dispenser upgrade plus ATM application work is a discrete second project. The 150-note bulk-deposit bundles confirm recycler-class note acceptors in the deposit-capable subset, which tells Printec what hardware generation it would be sitting alongside.
signals.followup: Establish whether EUR dispense is hardware- or licence-limited on the 201 RSD-only units; a licence-only constraint is a fast, cheap win.

signals.signal: SEPA euro payments went live at the bank on 05/05/2026: EUR transfers to SEPA countries execute same-day, incoming funds are credited immediately without waiting for supporting documentation, and routing between SEPA and SWIFT is automatic based on IBAN, currency and bank location with no client override.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka - SEPA sistem placanja (bank news)
signals.implies: Same-day, straight-through euro flows with immediate crediting materially raise the load on real-time sanctions screening and transaction monitoring - Printec AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring territory. New payment rails at a systemic bank are also a standard trigger for a monitoring-platform review.
signals.followup: Ask which transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening platform now covers the SEPA flow and whether it was extended or replaced for go-live.

signals.signal: NLB Group Q1 2026 presentation: NLB Komercijalna Banka has 391,309 active digital users at 31/03/2026, the Group's second largest digital base after NLB Ljubljana (498,554); the Group had more than 1.9 million digital users with a 2030 target of more than 80% digital penetration. Stated 2026 priorities include a relaunch of the NLB Klik app in Serbia, mobile-first biometric-based retail onboarding, a self-service digital onboarding model for legal entities, and 24/7 call centres rolled out across the Group.
signals.implies: Biometric mobile-first onboarding and legal-entity self-service onboarding are named 2026 deliverables - direct Printec digital onboarding / eKYC territory, and in Serbia they run against the NBS remote-identification framework. The Serbian Klik relaunch is a channel-integration moment that usually drags ATM and self-service journeys with it.
signals.followup: Probe whether the biometric onboarding stack is built in-house at Group level or sourced, and whether Serbia gets the Slovenian build or a local variant.

signals.signal: FY2025 (NLB Group AR2025, Table 22): total assets EUR 6,062.4m, result after tax EUR 153.8m, cost/income 40.8%, RoE 18.0%, NPL ratio 0.8%, market share by total assets 10.2%. Q1 2026: assets EUR 6,468.6m, result after tax EUR 33.0m, RoE 14.8%, cost/income 42.8%, gross loans +20% YoY (the largest increase of any Group bank), retail loans +21% YoY. The bank's own site cites a 9.8% market share and more than one million active clients.
signals.source_name: NLB Group Annual Report 2025; NLB Group Interim Report January-March 2026; nlbkb.rs About Us
signals.implies: Ample capacity and appetite to fund a self-service capex cycle. A cost/income ratio already in the low 40s combined with the >90%-off-branch target pushes the bank toward automation rather than headcount, which is the commercial frame for a recycler and 24/7-zone programme.
signals.followup: Watch the NLB Group H1 2026 earnings call on 06/08/2026 for any network or self-service disclosure.

signals.signal: The OEM/vendor of the 304-unit multifunctional ATM fleet remains UNDISCLOSED after a fresh multi-angle search this run: bank website and ATM functionality pages, the four published ATM-location PDFs, the AEM locator API, the page model JSON, NLB KB Pillar 3 31/12/2025, NLB Group AR2025 (full text search for Diebold, Nixdorf, NCR, Atleos, Hyosung, Wincor, Printec, Payten, ASEE, Auriga, KAL, CR2, Glory, Vynamic, SelfServ - zero hits), NLB Group Q1 2026 report and presentation, and Serbian and English press. The July 2022 replacement announcement names no supplier.
signals.source_name: Telegraf Biznis (original 2022 replacement announcement), cross-checked against all bank and Group primary sources listed
signals.implies: Standing intelligence gap, now narrowed: the 2025 Group-level ATM and CDS tenders mean the incumbent question is a GROUP question, answerable in Ljubljana rather than Belgrade. Remaining routes are the ATM fascia/screen branding in the field, NBS outsourcing and critical-service-provider filings, and Serbian systems-integrator reference lists.
signals.followup: Operator task: photograph an NLB KB ATM fascia and welcome screen in Belgrade to read the OEM badge and ATM application branding.

signals.signal: The public website embeds a live video-banking channel served from nlb.nexios.io (a third-party chat/video platform), configured for chat and video in Serbian, alongside 1,627 partner merchant locations listed for card instalment purchases.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka page model JSON (footer configuration) and locator endpoint
signals.implies: Remote-advisory tooling is already outsourced to a third party, so the remote-channel stack is contestable at renewal - and video is the assisted-service layer that a >90%-off-branch target depends on. The 1,627-merchant instalment estate sizes the acquiring/POS footprint Printec could address.
signals.followup: Confirm the Nexios contract scope and whether remote onboarding/eKYC sits inside it or is a separate contract.

signals.signal: Unaudited H1 2026 statutory statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, off-balance-sheet positions as at 30/06/2026) are already published on the bank's investor page, ahead of the NLB Group H1 2026 earnings call scheduled for 06/08/2026.
signals.source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka - Finansijski izvestaji (quarterly unaudited statements, 2026 folder); NLB Group financial calendar
signals.implies: Next disclosure window for any network, ATM or IT-investment commentary is 06/08/2026 - one week after this run. Any Printec approach should be timed to land just after it.
signals.followup: Re-run this bank immediately after 06/08/2026 to capture H1 2026 network and digitalisation commentary.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Primary sources actually opened: (1) nlbkb.rs ATM functionality page plus its four ATM-location PDFs, downloaded and text-extracted locally with pdfminer (pdftotext is not installed on this machine) - derived counts of 181 RSD/EUR-deposit, 97 EUR-dispense, 112 merchant-deposit and 233 QR locations; (2) the bank's AEM locator endpoint branchsearch.facilities.json, discovered by reading the site clientlib JS for Sling selectors after .model.json and /bin/ probes returned 400/404 - this returned the full 2,151-record facility set (304 ATM, 129 branch, 91 CDS, 1,627 merchant) with per-device capability flags, which is far richer and fresher than the PDFs and is the basis for the headline numbers; (3) NLB KB Pillar 3 'Objavljivanje podataka i informacija' 31/12/2025 PDF (139 branches, 2,153 staff); (4) NLB KB quarterly statements index showing H1-2026 statements already filed; (5) NLB Group Interim Report Q1 2026 PDF; (6) NLB Group Presentation Q1 2026 PDF; (7) NLB Group Annual Report 2025 ENG PDF (17MB, full text extracted) - source of the ATM/CDS tender finalisation and the 2030 ATM accessibility commitment; (8) NLB Group IR and financial-reports pages; (9) NBS payment statistics workbooks prihvatna_mreza.xlsx and trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx, fetched with a desktop User-Agent and parsed with openpyxl; (10) nlbkb.rs news index and the SEPA and daily-limit news items. Search angles varied deliberately: Serbian-language press, the bank's own AEM content APIs, Group IR PDFs, the regulator's raw statistical workbooks, and full-text vendor-name search across the Group annual report. Genuine gaps: (a) the ATM OEM is still not named - a full-text search of AR2025 for fifteen vendor names returned zero hits, and the 2022 announcement names no supplier; (b) the winner and term of the 2025 Group ATM/CDS tenders is not disclosed; (c) the 129-vs-139 branch discrepancy between the locator and the reported figure is unresolved; (d) the 181 vs 202 deposit-capable ATM discrepancy between the published PDFs and the live locator is unresolved - the PDFs are probably stale, so the locator figure is used and the PDF figure is not reported as fact; (e) no NLB Group Investor Day 07/05/2026 deck was found on the public IR pages; (f) the pairing of banks to digital-penetration percentages in the Q1 2026 presentation chart could not be resolved reliably from the extracted text, so only the absolute user count for NLB KB is reported. All confidence values are capped at Medium per the rules.
access_issues: www.nlbkb.rs blocks the plain fetch tool for JSON endpoints; resolved by using curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent. The AEM component endpoints .../branchsearch.model.json and .../branchsearch.branches.json return HTTP 400 and /bin/nlb/branches.json returns 404 - the working route is the .facilities.json Sling selector on the component path under /content/nlbbanks/..., found by grepping the site clientlib bundle. nbs.rs served fine with a desktop User-Agent (no 403 encountered). pdftotext is not installed locally, so all PDFs were extracted with pdfminer.six. No source was silently dropped.
operator_requests: 1) Field check, Belgrade: photograph the fascia and welcome screen of two or three NLB Komercijalna ATMs (for example Kneza Mihaila 38, Bulevar Mihajla Pupina 165v, Nikola Tesla Airport hall) to read the OEM badge and the ATM application branding - this is the fastest remaining route to naming the incumbent. 2) Ask NLB Group procurement in Ljubljana who won the ATM and Cash Deposit Machine (CDS) tenders finalised in 2025, and the framework term and call-off mechanics. 3) Check National Bank of Serbia supervisory filings for outsourcing / critical service provider notifications by NLB Komercijalna banka covering ATM operation and maintenance.
